“Blocked Fallopian Tubes? IVF Can Help.”

Many women struggle to conceive because their fallopian tubes are blocked or damaged.

Normally, the egg and sperm meet inside the fallopian tube.
But when the tube is blocked, the sperm cannot reach the egg.

✨ How IVF helps:

Eggs are collected directly from the ovaries

Fertilization happens in the laboratory

The embryo is placed directly into the uterus

This bypasses the fallopian tubes completely, giving couples a real chance at pregnancy.

🌱 IVF Success Starts With the Right Timing

⏰ When Should You Seek Fertility Help?

Many couples wait too long before consulting a fertility specialist. Early evaluation can **save time, reduce stress, and improve success rates.**

👉 Consider consulting a fertility expert if:

✔️ Trying for **1 year without pregnancy** (age <35)

**Strategies to Improve Egg Quality and Number of Eggs**

Egg quality and egg number are crucial factors for successful conception, whether natural or through IVF. Egg number mainly depends on age and ovarian reserve, while egg quality reflects the genetic and metabolic health of the egg. Although new eggs cannot be created, the quality of existing eggs can be improved by optimizing the body’s internal environment.

A healthy lifestyle forms the foundation of good egg health. A balanced diet rich in proteins, antioxidants, fruits, vegetables, nuts, and healthy fats helps reduce oxidative stress on eggs. Maintaining an ideal body weight, avoiding smoking, alcohol, and excess caffeine, and ensuring adequate sleep are equally important. Stress reduction through yoga, meditation, or regular physical activity supports hormonal balance.

Medical optimization also plays a key role. Treating thyroid disorders, insulin resistance, and hormonal imbalances improves ovulation and ovarian response. Supplements such as CoQ10, myo-inositol, vitamin D, and omega-3 fatty acids may enhance egg quality when taken under medical supervision.

In IVF, individualized stimulation protocols, correct dosing, and precise timing can improve the number of mature eggs retrieved. Ultimately, improving egg quality and number is a gradual process, and early, personalized fertility care offers the best chance of success.
How to Improve Endometrial Thickness:

For pregnancy to occur, the uterus needs a healthy inner lining called the endometrium, where the embryo attaches and grows. In some women, this lining remains thin despite medicines, hormones, or fertility treatments. A thin endometrium can reduce the chances of embryo implantation, especially during IVF.

Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) are an advanced treatment option for women who do not respond to routine therapies. These special cells have the ability to repair and regenerate damaged tissues. They are usually obtained from safe sources such as the placenta or umbilical cord.

When MSCs are introduced into the uterus, they help improve blood flow, reduce scarring, and promote the growth of healthy endometrial tissue. Unlike treatments that work temporarily, MSC therapy aims to improve the overall quality of the uterine lining.

This therapy may benefit women with very thin endometrium, scarring after infections or surgery, or repeated IVF failures due to poor endometrial growth. MSC therapy is considered a specialized option and is recommended only after proper evaluation and counseling by a fertility specialist.

To the doctors who brought the blessings in our life
And then there are people who quietly become your strength when you are at your weakest.
Our journey to parenthood was not a straight road. It was a sea — uncertain, emotional, exhausting in ways only those who have walked the path of fertility truly understand. And in that vast ocean, two hands held our boat steady:

Dr. Sonali Gulhane Raut and Dr. Ankush Raut.

We first met Dr. Sonali at Shreesha Women Care. There was no rush in her voice. No clinical detachment. She listened — truly listened. Not just to reports and numbers, but to fears, exhaustion, and years of silent hope. It was she who guided us to consult Dr. Ankush at Apollo Fertility Borivali, and that moment quietly changed our lives.
From day one, we never felt like “patients.” We never felt like a case file in a corporate system. They understood — deeply — the mental strain, the physical toll, and yes, even the financial burden that couples silently carry in the fertility world. In an industry that can often feel mechanical and transactional, they remained profoundly human.
They did not treat us like clients navigating a medical service.
They treated us like family fighting for a dream.
There were countless moments when they went beyond duty — late replies, patient explanations, calm reassurance when anxiety was loud. The journey of high risk pregnancy is never easy with preeclampsia, and other challenges. But they supported us mentally and medically to face it. But one moment will stay etched in my heart forever.
After delivery, when Priyanka had to be transferred to another hospital’s ICU, everything felt fragile. Time felt heavy. Fear felt real. And in that ambulance, it was Dr. Sonali who sat beside me — not as a doctor fulfilling responsibility, but as someone sharing our burden. And before we even reached, Dr. Ankush was already there at the ICU, ensuring everything was ready so not even a second would be lost.
Who does that in today’s world?
In a time where medicine is often overshadowed by materialism, doctors like them are not just rare — they are gems. They remind you why this profession is sacred. Why the word “doctor” once carried the weight of trust, compassion, and quiet heroism.
To us, they were not just the captain and co-captain of our pregnancy journey —
they were the steady compass when we were losing direction.
We believe more aspiring parents — especially those who have waited for years and almost given up — deserve to know that such doctors exist. That there are still healers who combine science with soul.
With folded hands and a heart full of gratitude —
thank you for sailing us to parenthood with dignity, grace, and unwavering care.
Forever grateful.

What is the Difference Between PCOD and PCOS? 🤔
Many people use PCOD and PCOS interchangeably, but they are not exactly the same.
🌸 PCOD (Polycystic Ovarian Disease) is a condition where the ovaries contain multiple immature follicles. Many women have mild symptoms, and with healthy lifestyle changes, ovulation and fertility can often improve.
🌸 PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome) is a hormonal and metabolic disorder that can affect ovulation, menstrual cycles, fertility, and overall health. It may also be associated with acne, excessive hair growth, weight gain, insulin resistance, and irregular periods.
Common symptoms include: ✅ Irregular or missed periods
✅ Acne and oily skin
✅ Hair fall or excess facial hair
✅ Weight gain
✅ Mood changes
✅ Difficulty conceiving
The good news is that both PCOD and PCOS can be effectively managed with early diagnosis, healthy lifestyle changes, appropriate medications, and fertility treatment when needed.
Every woman is different, and treatment should always be personalized based on her symptoms and pregnancy goals.

Adenomyosis ≠ IVF for Everyone
Many women believe that a diagnosis of adenomyosis means IVF is the only option—but that's not true.
Treatment depends on several factors, including your age, symptoms, ovarian reserve (AMH), fallopian tube status, semen analysis, and pregnancy goals.
✅ Mild adenomyosis may be managed with medicines, timed intercourse, or IUI.
✅ Moderate cases require individualized treatment and close monitoring.
✅ Severe adenomyosis, low ovarian reserve, failed IUI, or increasing age may make IVF the most effective option. Sometimes, uterine preparation before IVF can further improve the chances of implantation.
The key is early evaluation and a personalized fertility plan. Don't delay seeking expert advice if you're planning a pregnancy.

What is SSG? 🌸

SSG (Saline Sonohysterography) is a special ultrasound test where saline is gently used to clearly see the inside of the uterus.

SSG helps detect:
✅ Uterine polyps
✅ Fibroids
✅ Adhesions or scars
✅ Causes of infertility
✅ Causes of recurrent pregnancy loss

A clear and healthy uterine cavity can improve the chances of implantation and pregnancy. Early diagnosis helps your fertility specialist plan the right treatment at the right time. 💛

At Sunrise Fertility & IVF Centre, we provide accurate fertility evaluation and personalized care for every couple’s parenthood journey.

When Should You Get an HSG Test? 🌸

An HSG (Hysterosalpingography) is a simple X-ray test that checks whether your fallopian tubes are open and evaluates the shape of your uterus. It is an important investigation for couples facing difficulty conceiving.

Your doctor may recommend an HSG if:
✅ You have been trying to conceive for 1 year without success (or 6 months if you are over 35)
✅ Pregnancy is not happening despite regular ovulation
✅ You are planning IUI treatment
✅ There is a suspicion of blocked fallopian tubes or unexplained infertility

Blocked fallopian tubes can prevent the egg and sperm from meeting, making natural conception difficult. Identifying the cause early helps your fertility specialist choose the most appropriate treatment.

💛 Early diagnosis leads to better fertility planning and improved chances of pregnancy.

What is Follicular Study? 🌸

Follicular study is a series of ultrasound scans done to track egg growth and identify the right time of ovulation.

It helps in:
✅ Knowing the exact ovulation day
✅ Tracking follicle/egg growth
✅ Timing intercourse or IUI correctly
✅ Improving chances of pregnancy

Right timing can make all the difference when you are trying to conceive. Follicular study helps identify your most fertile days and supports better fertility planning.
